---
title: "Histograms"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8.8, fig.height = 4.4, dpi = 100,
  fig.retina = 2, dev = "ragg_png", out.width = "100%"
)
options(gglaplot2.font = "inter")
library(ggplot2)
library(gglaplot2)
set.seed(1)
vals <- data.frame(x = c(rbeta(600, 2, 5), rbeta(400, 5, 2)),
                   group = rep(c("Inner London", "Outer London"), c(600, 400)))
```

A histogram is the bar mark with a binning stat: `geom_gla_bar(stat =
"bin")` gives the house bars with the surface hairline between bins. The
count axis is named, since it is not the measure in the subtitle.

## One distribution

```{r one}
ggplot(vals, aes(x)) +
  geom_gla_bar(stat = "bin", bins = 30, width = NULL) +
  gla_zero_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_gla_percent()) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = gla_breaks(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  gla_labs(title = "Most values sit below 50%", subtitle = "Distribution of a share, 1,000 areas",
           x = NULL, y = "Areas") +
  theme_gla(axis_titles = "y")
```

## Two, faceted

```{r two, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(vals, aes(x, fill = group)) +
  geom_gla_bar(stat = "bin", bins = 30, width = NULL) +
  gla_zero_line() +
  facet_wrap(vars(group), ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_gla() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_gla_percent()) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = gla_breaks(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  gla_labs(title = "Inner London sits lower", subtitle = "Distribution of a share by area",
           x = NULL, y = "Areas") +
  theme_gla(legend = "none", axis_titles = "y")
```

## Interactive

`gla_plotly()` turns the finished chart into an interactive one through
plotly. A histogram converts with its bars and panels; the hover label
reads the bin and the count.

```{r interactive, eval = requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE)}
gla_plotly(last_plot())
```
